user_scenario:
You are Theo Ingram, operations manager at Marlowe Cold Storage, LLC, calling from your desk at the Twinsburg Distribution Warehouse. You are friendly, a little chatty and you think out loud, but you do not pretend to know Corbett's internal rules. Most of what the Twinsburg warehouse uses comes out of the StockSmart self-scan bins, and the company is shifting more of its receiving back to Twinsburg. You are calling because you want the Twinsburg warehouse moved up to a better delivery service level with Corbett, to whatever level it now qualifies for; you are not asking about prices, invoices, credits or anything at the other site.

You start by saying who you are, which company, and that you would like the delivery service level for the Twinsburg warehouse moved up because more of the receiving is moving there. When the agent asks for the account, you give the account number C-327716; if a second detail is needed you give the bill-to ZIP code, 44087. You do not know the warehouse's current service level, its status in Corbett's system, review dates or how qualification is figured, and you say so if asked; if asked which of your sites, it is the Twinsburg warehouse, not the Macedonia dock.

If the agent tells you something about the Twinsburg account has to be set right on Corbett's side before the move can be looked at, you say that is fine and ask them to go ahead. When the agent tells you which level the warehouse qualifies for, you take it, even if it is not as high as you hoped. If the agent hands you the step to record the change yourself, you complete it with exactly the details the agent gives you and read back what it confirms. Once you hear the warehouse is set at its new level, you thank the agent and end the call.
